$system¶

Memory, disk and scratch-directory limits.

All limits apply per MPI process. For example, disk=10 on four processes can use 40 GB. For GGA DFT, the v5 documentation and a v8 benchmark report that most of the memory and all of the disk storage are used by the master process (rank 0). RI-MP2 and the other correlated methods write large scratch files on every process. In version 25, a two-process DFT run left one scratch file per process.

memory¶

Type: list
Default: 256
Units: MB
Status: current · verified on 25 (2025.02.28)
Sources: input.txt; 01 §4.1 (two values); 06 §3 (estimate); 03 §4, 04 #196 (per process); 08 t02, t58a

Default: echoed by version 25 when $system is omitted.

Memory limit in megabytes. A second value sets the limit for the other MPI ranks: mem=2048,256 gives rank 0 2048 MB and every other rank 256 MB. A single value applies to all ranks. The output echoes the result as Memory: <mem>m + <|disk|>m (<mem2>m + <|disk2|>m).

Note

For DFT, the v5 documentation estimates the memory as about 8·N²·3 bytes for energy and gradient, and twice that for an analytic Hessian, where N is the basis dimension. Dft.rtf gives an old default of 16 MB. Without a $system group, version 25 echoes Memory: 256m + 512m (256m + 512m), the same form that mem=512 disk=-512 gives. This is read as 256 MB of memory plus a 512 MB RAM disk per process (inferred from the echo format).

disk¶

Type: list
Default: -512
Status: current · verified on 25 (2025.02.28)
Sources: input.txt; Dft.rtf (one file per GB); 01 §4.1; 04 §0, #468; 03 §3, §17; 08 t02, t58a, t62, t64; 06 §3, 08 Slurm s02 (scratch per process)

Default: a 512 MB RAM disk (inferred from the version 25 echo Memory: 256m + 512m when $system is omitted).

Positive values set the disk space in gigabytes; one scratch file is opened per gigabyte, which sidesteps per-file size limits. Negative values set the amount of memory, in megabytes, used to emulate disk (a RAM disk). A second value applies to the other MPI ranks, as for memory; the official example inputs typically give them -1.

Note

With a RAM disk, memory plus |disk| (times the number of processes) must fit in physical RAM, or the run fails with malloc(...) failed. Example for a 24 GB node running a single process: memory=9000 disk=-14000. On one cluster, an RI-MP2 job on 8 cores with scratch in RAM ran 6× faster than on 2 cores with scratch on disk (a v8 benchmark; core count and scratch location both changed). In version 25, disk=-512 was echoed as Memory: 512m + 512m with no Disk: line, disk=1 as Disk:   1g '/tmp', and conventional MP2 with disk=-1 stopped with 0: out of disk space (grid_W).

Example:

$system mem=2048,256 disk=-256,-1 $end

path¶

Type: string
Default: none stated
Status: current · verified on 25 (2025.02.28)
Sources: input.txt; 03 §2; 04 #465; 08 t01, t64

Default: the TMPDIR environment variable, otherwise /tmp (version 25). input.txt says the current working directory.

Directory for temporary disk files. For parallel runs you can give a colon-separated list with one path per process: path=/tmpa:/tmpb:/tmpc:/tmpd makes process 1 write to /tmpa, process 2 to /tmpb, and so on. Those directories should be on different physical drives. The value may be double-quoted.

Note

For all methods except GGA DFT, performance degrades “terribly” if more than one process reads and writes large files on the same physical drive. Never put temporary files on NFS. On Windows (Cygwin), which has no /tmp, use path=.. Version 25, run without path=, used TMPDIR when it was set and /tmp when it was not (echo Disk:   1g '/tmp').

Example:

$system path=/tmpa:/tmpb:/tmpc:/tmpd $end
